messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed our JS SDK's types disappear when you install the edge sample app (vite + edge). Repro: `npm i @redwood/inference && import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'` and TS can't find types.

mj: hmm, seen that before with conditional exports. Can you paste package.json exports?

alex: sure — from the installed package: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./runtime": {
    "edge": "dist/edge.mjs"
  }
},
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```

sara: suspect is that bundlers/TS use the export map conditionals and ignore top-level "types" in some resolver flows. TS expects a "types" or "types" conditional inside exports (or a `exports"."."types"` entry). Edge runtimes that use native ESM resolution can end up not seeing the d.ts.

ryan: TL;DR — some tooling (vite, esbuild, bun) will resolve the module via the `import` entry and then look for an adjacent `index.d.ts` or `types` field but conditional exports can confuse it. We need to add explicit "types" condition inside exports for all entry points.

nia: example fix?

mj: something like: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./runtime": {
    "types": "dist/runtime.d.ts",
    "edge": "dist/edge.mjs"
  }
}
```

alex: can also hit issues with `package.json#module` vs `exports` — some older Node versions fall back to `module` and pick the wrong file for edge. The sample app uses `vite` which loads the `import` path but TS still needs the `types` pointer.

ryan: Another gotcha: when we publish with `files`/packlist, ensure .d.ts files are included at those exact paths. CI sometimes strips them if globbing is wrong. I opened an earlier accidental release where dist/*.d.ts was not included.

ci-bot: CI check: publish-packlist check failed on 1791220000 — missed: dist/index.d.ts in release v0.8.3.

alex: Ugh — that explains why some users reported missing types intermittently. But the edge sample app error we've seen locally persists even after verifying d.ts exists in package. So both problems.

mj: For the edge app we need two changes: 1) add exports.types conditional per entry 2) include a `types` top-level as fallback for legacy tooling. Example: 
```json
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"exports": {".": {"types": "dist/index.d.ts","import": "dist/index.mjs","require": "dist/index.cjs"},"./runtime": {"types":"dist/runtime.d.ts","edge":"dist/edge.mjs"}}
```

ria: (typo — ryan) also consider adding a small README snippet for sample apps: "If you see TS errors after install, try clearing node_modules + lockfile or pin npm >=7/node >=16". Many onboarding tickets are solved by stale lockfiles.

nia: I tried clearing lockfile and it still failed until I validated the d.ts shipped. So both are definitely in the wild.

alex: One more wrinkle — edge runtime imports our `./runtime` entry which only has `edge` conditional. Tools like bundlers sometimes prefer the `edge` condition and then TS resolution doesn't check that branch for types. We should add `import` alias for browser/edge too: 
```json
"./runtime": { "types": "dist/runtime.d.ts", "import": "dist/runtime.mjs", "edge": "dist/edge.mjs" }
```

mj: Agreed. Plan: patch release that updates package.json exports and run a smoke test on the vite sample app + node script that imports from the SDK. Also add a new CI lint that validates `exports` contains `types` for every exported key.

sara: can we also add a TS test in the sample apps folder that runs `tsc --noEmit` to catch regressions in CI? Quick to run and high signal.

ryan: I'll draft the PR. PR checklist:
- add types fields to exports
- ensure dist/*.d.ts included in packlist
- add sample-app tsc check to CI (only runs on package changes)
- update CHANGELOG and add note in docs troubleshooting

alex: ping me for a quick review. Also, we should mention this in onboarding docs (DX) — a short blurb under "Edge runtimes & types". We've gotten 3 support tickets this month.

nia: do we need to worry about CJS consumers? Adding `types` shouldn't break CJS, but make sure require path still points to .cjs.

mj: correct. Order inside each conditional doesn't matter, but keep them explicit. Also add a fallback export for `./package.json` if consumers try to read it? Not necessary now.

ryan: opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/472 — includes tests and a failing sample-app run before the patch, passing after.

alex: amazing. after merge can we cut v0.8.4 patch and push a quick sample-app smoke release tag so docs link to a working example?

ci-bot: release pipeline queued for v0.8.4 after PR merge.

sara: Nice catch. This is exactly the kind of onboarding friction we need to scrub before GA.

alex: OK — thanks all. I'll update the dev-experience doc and add a short note to onboarding checklist. :white_check_mark:

ryan: will also add a small repro in the issue so support can point users to it.

alex: closing the loop here. If anyone still sees issues after v0.8.4, please drop the exact `npm ls @redwood/inference` + `node -v` + `tsc --version` in the thread.
